loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: Every family has its own way of living. Don't let outside gossip cause hurt between you; trust and stand by one another.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Praise and criticism at work are normal. Take useful feedback, let groundless remarks pass and keep working with a calm mind.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: A steady mind supports a healthy body. Keep regular routines and read less negative news. When stress builds up, find someone to talk to.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Don't let comparisons with friends discourage you. Pursue your goals at a pace that suits you.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Trust your sincere feelings more than rumors. A steady relationship needs trust from both sides.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Don't chase spending or investment trends out of fear of falling behind. Stick to your own financial plan; steady is enough.

loiKhuyen: Listen to feedback, but hold firm to what you believe is right. A mountain doesn't move for the wind.
ghiChu: This verse is for reflection, to help you look within; it is not a prediction.

tho: For years away from pier and lane
Now home, the bamboo stands again
The old pier waits, as patient still
With laughter, warmth, and old goodwill
loiGiai: After many years away from the landing and the village, you return to find the bamboo row still standing, the old pier still waiting and familiar laughter sheltering the whole family. This verse carries a feeling of reunion and gratitude for your roots. However far you go, your old home and loved ones remain your support. Make time to return, visit and keep those bonds alive.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: This is a good time to visit your hometown, your grandparents and parents. If you cannot go yet, a caring phone call is enough to make your family happy.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: You may meet old acquaintances or former colleagues again. Keep these relationships warm; sincere bonds often open doors.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: The air of home and a meal cooked by family help the spirit recover. Give yourself time to rest, and remind relatives to have health check-ups.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Don't forget the teachers and schools that taught you. A visit or a note of thanks also nourishes your love of learning.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Love can come from what is familiar and close. Treasure the person who has always been by your side, even when you were far away.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Set aside part of your money to care for your family. Plan your spending so that trips home are always joyful and easy.

loiKhuyen: Call a loved one today, or set a date to visit. Your old home always has someone waiting.
ghiChu: This verse is for reflection, to help you look within; it is not a prediction.

tho: Into good earth a seed is sown today
Through rain and sun it sprouts in its own way
A steady heart is like that seed below
With patient care, tomorrow's roots will grow
loiGiai: This verse speaks of a seed just planted. It lies still beneath the soil, nothing yet shows above ground, but inside it has already begun to grow. Your current efforts are the same: what you put in today may not show results right away. Don't dig up the seed to check whether it has sprouted. Keep watering, keep the soil moist, and in time the shoot will rise on its own. Today's perseverance is the foundation for tomorrow.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: The good things you nurture at home, such as gentle words, shared meals and small acts of care, may not change things overnight, but they are quietly taking root. Keep going.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: A new project or plan is in its planting stage. Work steadily, track your progress, and don't lose heart if results don't appear in the first few weeks.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Good habits like sleeping earlier, walking and eating more vegetables take time to show their effect. Keep them up, and consult a doctor if anything feels unusual.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Knowledge gathered day by day is like a seed in the soil. Reviewing a little every day is sturdier than cramming before an exam.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: A good relationship needs time for two people to understand each other. Don't rush it; let feelings grow naturally through sincerity.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Money comes from diligence and steady saving. Set aside a small amount each month, and over time it will become a solid reserve.

loiKhuyen: Today, choose one small, useful task and do it every day, as if watering a seed.
ghiChu: This verse is for reflection, to help you look within; it is not a prediction.

tho: A tender sprout peeks out beside the wall
The wind may bend it; rooted, it won't fall
Sleep soundly, so the roots grow deep and strong
And calm will keep the leaves green all year long
loiGiai: A young sprout is still soft and bends in the wind, yet its roots hold firm so it stays upright. This verse reminds you to care for your own roots: sleep, meals and a calm heart. Tiredness is sometimes a reminder to slow down. Rest isn't laziness; it gives your roots time to grow deep. When the base is healthy, the plant will rise green and strong on its own.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: People at home get tired too. Share the housework, let each other rest, so everyone keeps their strength.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Don't take on too much at once. Schedule proper breaks; good health is what makes your work last.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Your body needs care right now. Sleep enough, drink water, move gently. If fatigue lasts or unusual symptoms appear, see a doctor early.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Studying late night after night tires the mind. Alternate study time with rest; a well-rested mind remembers better.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Take care of yourself first. Someone who is kind to themselves knows how to love others more gently.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Don't trade your health for extra income. Work within your strength; spending on wholesome meals and good sleep is a sound investment.

loiKhuyen: Tonight, go to bed a little earlier than usual, and keep your phone away from the bed.
ghiChu: This verse is for reflection, to help you look within; it is not a prediction.

tho: A lotus rises pink from muddy ground
Its fragrance pure, its color clear and sound
A gentle soul keeps one heart true and bright
Untouched by dust, it walks the days in light
loiGiai: The lotus grows out of mud yet keeps its fragrance and its color. This verse encourages you to keep an upright heart even when things around you aren't as you wish. You don't need to change the whole pond; you only need to keep your own heart clear. When you live kindly, others will gradually feel it, just as lotus fragrance travels far without anyone announcing it.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: When there is disagreement at home, be the one who keeps their words calm. One person's composure can soften the whole atmosphere.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Your workplace may be complicated, but stay honest and dedicated. Trust is built from doing the right thing every day.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: A clear mind helps the body feel light. Take in less negativity, and spend time in nature and with people who bring you peace.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Study on your own merit and never cheat. Results may come a little slower, but they will truly be yours and they will last.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Love with sincerity rather than pretending to please someone. The right person will treasure that very clarity.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Earn your money honestly. Stay away from vague get-rich-quick offers; only rightful earnings stay with you for long.

loiKhuyen: When something annoys you today, take three deep breaths before you answer, and keep your words gentle.
ghiChu: This verse is for reflection, to help you look within; it is not a prediction.

tho: The apricot has yet to bloom this year
Don't grieve: the buds are swelling, spring is here
A later bloom is never far away
When sunlight comes, gold fills the branch one day
loiGiai: Some apricot branches bloom early and some bloom late, yet every one of them turns bright gold once it has enough sun. This verse comforts you if you feel you are behind others. Everyone has their own season. Instead of comparing, tend to your own buds: learn more, work steadily and stay patient. Good things that come late are still good, and are often treasured all the more.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: Hopes for your family, such as repairing the house or a full reunion, may need more time. Prepare slowly and don't blame yourself.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: A promotion may come later than you planned. Keep sharpening your skills so that you are ready when the chance arrives.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Everyone recovers at their own pace. Follow your doctor's advice, be patient with your body, and don't rush.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Some people grasp a lesson quickly and some need more time. Learning slowly but surely beats learning fast and forgetting.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Whether love comes early or late doesn't decide your happiness. Live joyfully and kindly; the right person will notice you at the right time.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Your finances are improving slowly. Keep saving, and avoid borrowing to keep up with others. Step by step, you will stand firm.

loiKhuyen: For one day, stop comparing yourself to others, and write down one way you have grown.
ghiChu: This verse is for reflection, to help you look within; it is not a prediction.

tho: Green bamboo stands together, side by side
Through wind and rain, their roots are knit and tied
A home that keeps its words both kind and mild
Finds harmony from grandparent to child
loiGiai: A single bamboo stalk is easily battered by the wind, but a whole hedge standing close together cannot be knocked down even by a storm. Underground, their roots weave into one another and hold each other up. This verse speaks of the strength of togetherness. In a family or a group, when people give way to each other, speak kindly and lend a hand, even hard things can be overcome.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: This is a time to nurture family bonds. Call a relative you haven't seen in a while, share a meal, and say thank you or sorry when needed.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Teamwork will go better than working alone. Share information, help your colleagues, and move forward together.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Having someone beside you steadies your spirit. Invite family to exercise with you and remind each other of good habits.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Studying with friends deepens understanding. Form a study group, explain things to each other, and help where you are strong.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Love lasts when two people stand on the same side in hard times. Listen and stay united instead of trying to win.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: When the family plans spending together, waste is avoided. Being open about money helps everyone feel at ease.

loiKhuyen: Today, do one small thing to help someone at home without being asked.
ghiChu: This verse is for reflection, to help you look within; it is not a prediction.

tho: A bamboo shoot pushes up through the earth
Each day a joint, it grows to its full worth
So learn a little, listen as you go
And one day you'll give shade to those below
loiGiai: A tiny bamboo shoot is strong enough to push through a layer of soil and rise. Each day it grows one more joint, never hurrying and never stopping. This verse is for those who are learning or just starting out. Don't worry that you are still young or new; just move forward a little each day, listen well and work hard, and you will become a sturdy bamboo that gives shade to others.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: The children in the family are growing and need encouragement more than scolding. Elders, guide patiently; young ones, listen.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: If you are new to the job, learn humbly from those before you. Each small task done well is one more sturdy joint.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Build health bit by bit: a few more minutes of movement each day, one more serving of vegetables, one less sugary drink.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: A good time to learn something new. Break goals into small parts, master one piece each day, and ask your teacher when unsure.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: New feelings need sincerity and respect. Get to know each other step by step, and don't rush into promises.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Start learning to manage money with small amounts. Recording income and spending helps you understand yourself and improve.

loiKhuyen: Learn one new thing today, even for just fifteen minutes, and write down what you have understood.
ghiChu: This verse is for reflection, to help you look within; it is not a prediction.

tho: Row after row, the young rice plants go in
With honest sweat, the greening fields begin
Work straight and true, with sincere heart and hand
And harvest time brings full grain to the land
loiGiai: A farmer planting rice bends low to set each seedling, evenly and carefully. The work is hard, but green fields are the first reward. This verse advises diligence and working with an honest heart. Don't look for shortcuts; do each part of the job thoroughly. When the season comes, your effort will turn into full, firm grain.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: When everyone lends a hand with housework, no one carries it all. The whole family's diligence makes a warm, full home.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: This stage calls for hard, careful work. Finish each part with care, and the results will be worthy of your effort.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Work hard, but remember to stretch, drink water and take breaks. Keep your back straight so your health stays with you.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: No study method replaces hard work. Do all your exercises, review your mistakes, and exam season will feel lighter.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Love needs tending too: a caring question, a thoughtful deed. Don't let the one you love feel forgotten.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Income comes from real effort. Work diligently, spend with a plan, and stay away from gambling and promises of unusually high returns.

loiKhuyen: Pick the most important task today and finish it properly before moving on to anything else.
ghiChu: This verse is for reflection, to help you look within; it is not a prediction.

tho: In golden fields the heavy grain bows low
So full, yet quiet, never making show
When you have much, don't boast of what you've done
Stay humble as the rice beneath the sun
loiGiai: The more grain a rice stalk carries, the lower it bends; it never shows off, yet everyone values it. This verse comes when you have achieved something or soon will. Enjoy what you have gained, but stay humble. Remember those who helped you, and never look down on others. Humility keeps you learning and helps you keep what you have.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: As life gets better, remember the parents and siblings who supported you. Share your joy gently, without claiming credit.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: A good result is a time to credit the whole team. People who stay humble are trusted with bigger tasks.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Even when healthy, don't be careless. Keep up regular check-ups and the good habits that brought you here.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: The more you learn, the more you see what you lack. Good grades are a joy, but keep asking, keep exploring, and help your classmates.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Don't show off or keep score in love. Simplicity and honesty make the other person feel closer to you.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Once you have some savings, spend simply and keep a reserve for when it is needed. No boasting, no splurging, and it will last.

loiKhuyen: Today, send a thank-you to someone who helped make your achievement possible.
ghiChu: This verse is for reflection, to help you look within; it is not a prediction.

tho: Behind the house a little garden grows
At dawn and dusk my mother tends the rows
A simple meal, but full of love and care
Fresh greens, soft rice; not much, yet joy is there
loiGiai: A small vegetable patch behind the house, tended every day, gives meals that are fresh and clean. This verse reminds you that happiness often lies in simple things: wholesome food, enough sleep, family gathered close. There is no need to search far away; take good care of what you already have. Peace begins in your own kitchen and under your own roof.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: Cook a meal together and sit down to eat with phones put away. Such simple moments make family bonds warmer.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Your current steady job deserves appreciation. Do your part well, and don't let comparison take away your peace.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Eat more greens, less fried food, and sleep on time. Small changes in your meals bring lasting benefits to your body.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: A tidy study corner and regular hours help learning settle into a routine. Eat a proper breakfast before class to keep a clear head.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Love shines in small things: cooking a dish for each other, tidying up together. Simple, yet warm.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Save from your own kitchen: cook at home more often, buy only what you need, and waste nothing. Small sums add up.

loiKhuyen: Today, cook a simple meal with fresh greens yourself and invite a family member to share it.
ghiChu: This verse is for reflection, to help you look within; it is not a prediction.

tieuDe: The Old Tree at the Village Gate
tho: Beside the village gate, the old tree stands
Its shade a gift from long-departed hands
Remember those who planted it with care
Enjoy its shade, and plant another there
loiGiai: The shade of the old tree today exists because people long ago planted it. This verse reminds you to be grateful to grandparents, parents, teachers and all who came before. Gratitude isn't only in words but in carrying on: preserving the good they left and planting more good for those who follow. When you plant a tree, you are giving shade to the future.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: Spend time visiting grandparents and parents. Listen to their stories of the old days and write down the family's precious lessons.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Learn from those who came before you in your field, and once you are steady, be willing to guide newcomers.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Check on the health of elderly relatives and take them for regular check-ups. Caring for yourself also eases the load on future generations.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Honor your teachers by studying seriously. The knowledge you receive today is the work of many generations.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Love lasts when you cherish each other's families. Respect and care for the parents of the one you love.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Whatever your elders left you, large or small, keep it and use it wisely. At the same time, save on your own for the next generation.

loiKhuyen: Today, call or visit an older person you feel grateful to.
ghiChu: This verse is for reflection, to help you look within; it is not a prediction.

tho: A sparrow pecks for grain beside the stair
Seed after seed, it builds its nest with care
Spend wisely, and keep back a little more
And patient years will fill your family's store
loiGiai: The little sparrow is never greedy; it picks only a few grains at a time, yet thanks to its diligence the nest stays warm. This verse speaks of saving and knowing what is enough. You don't need large windfalls; set aside a little each day and spend with thought, and you will build a solid reserve. That is how you keep yourself and your family secure.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: Plan this month's spending together as a family, and teach children the habit of saving even small coins.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Success at work is built from small tasks done well each day. Don't overlook the little jobs.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Health is also something you accumulate. Walk a little and sleep a little better each day; in time your body will thank you.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Learn a few words or formulas every day, and after a few months you will be surprised how much you know.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Love is nurtured by small things like a caring message or a goodnight wish. Steady and sincere.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: A good time to build an emergency fund. Set aside part of your income as soon as you are paid, limit impulse buys, and never borrow to spend.

loiKhuyen: Today, put a small amount into a piggy bank or savings account, even if the sum is very small.
ghiChu: This verse is for reflection, to help you look within; it is not a prediction.

tho: The swallows circle back through skies of blue
They bring the spring, and buds bloom fresh and new
The house is bright with laughter and with cheer
On the long road, a friend is walking near
loiGiai: When the swallows return, spring has arrived; trees put out new shoots and hearts feel light. This verse carries the air of a fresh start. You may soon meet new people, take on new work, or find a new way of seeing things. Open your heart to it, while still weighing things carefully. A long road feels lighter with a companion, so cherish those who come to you with goodwill.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: There may be happy news at home or relatives coming back to gather. Prepare a welcoming and open heart.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: A chance for collaboration or a new project may appear. Look into it carefully and prepare well before you say yes.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: A fresh start for good habits: try a gentle sport, step out into the morning sun, and breathe in clean air.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: A good time to start a new course or subject. Find a study partner to keep your motivation up.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: If you are single, you may meet someone compatible through friends or work. If you are a couple, try something new together.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: New opportunities call for caution. Look into the details clearly, and don't put all your savings into something uncertain.

loiKhuyen: This week, take the first step to greet or get to know someone new, with sincerity.
ghiChu: This verse is for reflection, to help you look within; it is not a prediction.

tho: A little fish swims up the mountain stream
Though fins grow tired, it won't give up its dream
Review your lessons every single day
With steady will, your mind will find its way
loiGiai: A little fish swims against the current; its fins are still young and the water is strong, yet it keeps going bit by bit. This verse is for anyone struggling with study or training. Swimming upstream is tiring, but that very effort makes you stronger. Rest when you need to, then swim on. Each time you pass a hard stretch, you understand more and stand steadier.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: Your family needs everyone's patience right now. Encourage each other through this difficult stretch rather than blaming.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Work brings many challenges. Break problems into parts, solve them one at a time, and don't hesitate to ask experienced people.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Build physical training gradually without overexerting. Listen to your body, rest when tired, and see a doctor if pain persists.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: A hard subject isn't frightening if you review it daily. Redo the problems you got wrong, ask teachers or friends, and you will see progress.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: A little turbulence in love is normal. Talk patiently and find a way together to understand and move past it.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: If money is tight, keep trimming unnecessary spending and look for ways to improve your skills to earn more honestly.

loiKhuyen: Choose the hardest part of today's studies, work on it for twenty-five minutes, then reward yourself with a break.
ghiChu: This verse is for reflection, to help you look within; it is not a prediction.

tho: In a clear pond the fish swim slow and free
They don't chase the waves or crave the sea
Want less, and let your worries ebb away
Live fully now, at ease from day to day
loiGiai: Fish in a small pond still swim at ease; they don't need a vast ocean to be happy. This verse advises you to know what is enough and to let go of needless worries. Often we are tired not because we lack something, but because we want too much or worry ahead about things that haven't happened. Live today fully and appreciate what you have; your heart will feel lighter and your days easier.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: Don't demand that your family be perfect. Accept what isn't quite as you wish, and home will have less tension and more laughter.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: You don't have to compete over everything. Focus on your own work, do it well and with a calm mind, and compare less.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Lasting anxiety affects sleep and health. Practice slow breathing, take walks, talk with someone you trust, and seek a counselor if needed.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Set realistic goals and don't put too much pressure on yourself. Learning with a relaxed mind helps you understand and remember longer.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Don't cling to or control the other person. Love that is natural and respectful lets both of you feel at ease.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Knowing what is enough is a kind of wealth. Spend within your means, and don't chase expensive things or investments promising quick profits.

loiKhuyen: Write down one worry you are carrying, then ask: what can I do about it today? Set the rest down for now.
ghiChu: This verse is for reflection, to help you look within; it is not a prediction.

tho: A cocoon rests where summer branches sway
On new-made wings, it flies off one fine day
The waiting time is shorter than it seems
Love fully, and the years will fill your dreams
loiGiai: The caterpillar rests in its cocoon for a while, as though nothing is happening, then one day becomes a butterfly flying through the garden. This verse speaks of transformation that needs time. In love and in yourself, there are quiet seasons for growing. Don't be impatient; use that time to understand and improve yourself, and you will come to others in a more beautiful way.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: Your family may be going through a change, such as moving house or welcoming a new member. Give each other time to adjust.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: You are in a period of transition or learning new work. Keep building your skills patiently, and don't judge yourself too soon.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Your body needs time to adapt to new habits. Keep them steady, notice how you feel, and ask a doctor when needed.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Some knowledge needs time to sink in. Don't lose heart if you don't understand at once; review it after a few days and it will become clear.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Don't rush in matters of the heart. Time spent getting to know each other helps two people see clearly. Love sincerely, and it will deepen over the years.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: A financial plan needs time to show results. Keep saving, and don't keep changing course just because you feel impatient.

loiKhuyen: Write down one thing you want to change about yourself and one small step to begin this week.
ghiChu: This verse is for reflection, to help you look within; it is not a prediction.

tho: The bees are humming in the morning light
Each has its task, and all work with delight
Shared work is lighter when we walk as one
With honey stored, give thanks for what's been done
loiGiai: In a beehive, each bee has its own job: some gather nectar, some build the comb, some guard the entrance. No one competes, and so the whole hive fills with sweet honey. This verse speaks of cooperation and responsibility. Do your own part well and respect the work of others. When success comes, don't forget to recognize each person's effort.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: Divide the housework clearly so everyone has a share. When each person contributes, the home stays tidy and no one feels hard done by.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Teamwork is the key right now. Clarify roles, coordinate smoothly, and praise colleagues when they do well.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Hard work is good, but even bees rest in the hive. Balance work with rest to keep your stamina.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Group study works when each person handles one part and shares it with the others. Don't let one friend carry it all.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Share responsibilities so neither of you carries everything alone. Thank each other for the small things every day.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Stable income comes from steady diligence. If you do business with others, keep clear records and be fair to one another.

loiKhuyen: Today, give a specific thank-you to a colleague or family member for something they did.
ghiChu: This verse is for reflection, to help you look within; it is not a prediction.

tho: A tall tree stands because its roots go deep
Through many storms, its ground it still will keep
A home's foundation is the love we share
Begun in childhood, it will still be there
loiGiai: A tree stands firm in a storm not because of its wide canopy but because its roots reach deep into the earth. For each of us, those roots are family and the values nurtured since childhood. This verse brings steadiness: however unsettled things are outside, return to your foundation. Keep your family ties, trust and kindness, and you will have solid ground to stand on.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: A good time to strengthen family ties. Look back on shared memories together, and keep common rituals like dinner or a weekend chat.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: When things shift, lean on a solid base: your core skills, your honesty and your good relationships.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: The foundation of health is eating, sleeping and moving. When you feel unsteady, return to keeping those three regular.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Master the fundamentals before advanced topics. Reviewing the basics will help you understand more deeply.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Lasting love rests on trust and respect. Keep your promises, even in the smallest things.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Put essentials and an emergency fund first before thinking of big purchases. A steady financial base brings a calm mind.

loiKhuyen: Tonight, spend a few minutes talking with a family member and ask them something you haven't asked in a long time.
ghiChu: This verse is for reflection, to help you look within; it is not a prediction.

tho: In autumn, leaves come drifting softly down
The tree lets go, so spring may bud its crown
Old troubles can be laid to rest at last
With a light heart, like clouds the days drift past
loiGiai: In autumn, the tree lets its yellow leaves fall without clinging to them, and that is why new buds can come next season. This verse reminds you about letting go. Some old matters, sorrows or grudges have passed, and carrying them only weighs the heart down. Letting go doesn't mean forgetting; it means allowing yourself to feel light, ready to welcome the fresh things waiting ahead.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: If there is an old grievance at home, be the first to let it go. One word of reconciliation can open a warmer atmosphere.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Past failures or mistakes are lessons, not burdens. Learn from them and step forward with a fresh mindset.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Holding sadness for a long time affects sleep and spirit. Share it with someone you trust, and seek a professional if needed.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: One poor exam doesn't define you. Look over what went wrong, then leave it behind and prepare for the next one.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: If a relationship has ended, gently wish that person well and give yourself time to heal. A new season will come.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Don't keep grieving a loss or try to win it back through risky moves. Accept it, learn from it, and start saving again.

loiKhuyen: Clear out a small corner of your home today, letting go of things you no longer use, and your heart will feel lighter too.
ghiChu: This verse is for reflection, to help you look within; it is not a prediction.

tho: At year's end, oranges weigh the branches low
Recall the hands that tended row by row
Pick them and share with neighbors far and near
For sweetness shared is sweetest of the year
loiGiai: After a year of care, the orange grove is heavy with fruit. This verse carries the joy of harvest: your effort is being, or will soon be, rewarded. Be glad of the results and remember the hard days behind you. What is more, joy is fuller when it is shared. Give to relatives, help neighbors; when sweet fruit is shared, human warmth grows deeper.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: Your family has joy to share. Celebrate simply together and thank everyone who contributed.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Your work is paying off after a period of effort. Credit the team and pass on what you have learned to others.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Your health is steady thanks to good habits. Keep them up and invite your loved ones to join in.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Your studies are going well. Share your methods with friends; helping others is also a way to review for yourself.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Your relationship is bearing fruit thanks to care. Thank your partner and share the joy with both families.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Your income is a little better. Save part of it, use part to care for your family, and help those in need as you are able.

loiKhuyen: Today, share something good you have, such as food, knowledge or time, with someone around you.
ghiChu: This verse is for reflection, to help you look within; it is not a prediction.

tho: Trim off the tangled branches you don't need
So all the sap can feed the shoot and seed
Do fewer things, but do each one with care
A lighter load will take you anywhere
loiGiai: A gardener prunes extra branches so the tree can focus its strength on the main shoots and bear better flowers and fruit. This verse advises you to rearrange your life: cut back on unnecessary tasks, promises beyond your strength, and habits that waste time. Doing less but doing it well is better than taking on everything and leaving it half done. When body and mind carry less, you will have the strength for a long journey.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: Simplify life at home: fewer extra things, fewer needless worries, so you have more time together.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: List your tasks and choose the most important ones. Learn to gently decline what goes beyond your capacity.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Your body is overloaded. Cut back on tasks, sleep enough, and reduce screen time. If exhaustion lasts, see a doctor.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Don't spread yourself over too many subjects at once. Choose a few key ones and learn them thoroughly.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Let go of keeping score and needless suspicion. Love feels lighter when you focus on what truly matters between you.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Review your spending and cut what is unnecessary, such as rarely used subscriptions or habitual shopping.

loiKhuyen: Write a to-do list, cross off one task that isn't truly needed, and give yourself that time to rest.
ghiChu: This verse is for reflection, to help you look within; it is not a prediction.

tieuDe: The White Egret in the Field
tho: An egret stands amid the distant field
On one leg, calm beside the golden yield
Let go: no hurry, nothing you must chase
Breathe slowly in the wide earth's open space
loiGiai: The white egret stands still in the field, calmly looking around without any hurry. This verse reminds you to live more slowly. A rushed pace easily tires the body and tenses the mind. Give yourself quiet moments: breathe deeply, take a walk, look at the sky. Slowing down doesn't set you back; it helps you see more clearly, work with a clearer head and stay healthy for longer.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: Spend an unhurried afternoon with family: a walk, a cup of tea, a chat. Relaxed hours bring loved ones closer.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Haste leads to mistakes. Slow down to check carefully, and think things through before important decisions.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Your body needs to relax. Practice slow breathing, stretch, and walk outdoors. If you are often stressed or sleepless, ask a doctor.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Learning slowly and thoroughly beats skimming. Reread each passage and summarize it in your own words.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Don't jump to conclusions about the other person. Take time to observe and listen, and your feelings will become clearer.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Don't make money decisions when you are rushed or anxious. Taking a few more days to think helps avoid unnecessary spending.

loiKhuyen: Today, spend five minutes sitting quietly, breathing slowly and paying attention only to your breath.
ghiChu: This verse is for reflection, to help you look within; it is not a prediction.

tho: In spring, pomelo blossoms scent the eaves
Their gentle fragrance drifts on through the leaves
True love has no need of a fancy phrase
Sincere and small, it warms the coming days
loiGiai: Pomelo blossoms are small and white, not dazzling, yet their soft fragrance fills the whole porch. This verse speaks of love that is simple yet deep. Love needs no flowery words or grand promises; it shows itself through steady, sincere care. Let your heart give off a gentle fragrance like pomelo blossoms, and those beside you will feel it.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: Show love to your family through small acts: brewing a pot of tea, asking a question, helping with a chore. No need for many words.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Quiet dedication will be noticed. Do your work well, treat colleagues kindly, and your reputation will spread on its own.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: A gentle spirit relaxes the body. Make time for small pleasures like tending plants or listening to soft music.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: You don't need to study loudly, just steadily and attentively. Quiet effort will bring results worth having.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Your relationship is in a lovely, tender phase. Be sincere, care in small ways, and don't rush or show off.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: You don't need lavish spending to show affection. A small gift chosen with heart means more than something expensive.

loiKhuyen: Today, do one small thing for someone you love without mentioning it, simply so they feel at ease.
ghiChu: This verse is for reflection, to help you look within; it is not a prediction.

tho: The gourd vine climbs its trellis, row on row
With friends close by to lean on, it can grow
When fruit is sweet, remember those who stayed
And lend your strength when others need your aid
loiGiai: A gourd vine cannot stand on its own, but with a bamboo trellis to support it, it climbs high, flowers and bears fruit. This verse reminds you that no one succeeds alone. Don't hesitate to ask for help when you need it, and learn humbly from teachers and friends. Once you have grown tall, remember those who were your trellis, and then, in turn, support others.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: Family is the sturdiest trellis. Don't hesitate to share difficulties with loved ones, and remember to return their help.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Find an experienced mentor or ask colleagues for feedback. Timely support helps you progress faster.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: When you are unwell, ask family for help and see a doctor. Accepting care isn't a weakness.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Ask teachers and friends when you don't understand. Studying with people more skilled than you helps you grow; remember to thank them.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Beautiful love is when two people support each other to grow. Encourage the dreams of the one you love.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Learn money management from people you trust. Avoid borrowing widely; if someone has helped you, repay on time.

loiKhuyen: Today, be brave and ask an experienced person about something you are stuck on, and thank them sincerely.
ghiChu: This verse is for reflection, to help you look within; it is not a prediction.

tieuDe: Tired Birds Return to the Nest
tho: At dusk the weary birds fly home to rest
And chirp once more within their old, warm nest
Though you may wander many miles away
Come home, where peace and loved ones always stay
loiGiai: As evening falls, birds tired from flying return to their old nest, where familiar chirping awaits. This verse brings to mind home and reunion. However far away or busy you are, remember there is a place always waiting for you to return. A phone call or a visit home can bring great joy to your family and peace to yourself.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: A good time for reunion. Plan a visit home or a family dinner with everyone. If you live far away, make a video call.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Don't let work sweep away all your family time. Rebalance your schedule so you can get home on time some evenings.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: When you are tired, return to places that put your heart at ease. Resting with loved ones helps your spirit recover.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Studying far from home can be lonely. Keep in touch with family and share your school life so they can encourage you.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Love grows steady when both of you look toward a shared home. Talk about your plans for the nest you will build together.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Budget sensibly to set aside money for trips home and family gatherings. That money is well spent.

loiKhuyen: Today, call your parents or a relative far away and ask them how they are.
ghiChu: This verse is for reflection, to help you look within; it is not a prediction.

tho: Along the road the wildflowers bloom with glee
With no one watching, sweet as they can be
There's no need to compare with anyone
Just bloom as you, at ease beneath the sun
loiGiai: The wildflower by the road is planted and tended by no one, yet it blooms brightly and gives off fragrance every morning. This verse encourages you to believe in your own worth. You don't need to be like anyone else or be praised to be precious. Live true to yourself, do your best with what you have, and enjoy your own kind of beauty. That gentle confidence will let you shine naturally.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: Each person at home has their own character. Respect the differences and praise each other's strengths instead of comparing.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Build on your own strengths rather than trying to copy others. Being different can be an advantage.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Don't force yourself into someone else's mould. Care for your body in a way that suits you, and follow your doctor's advice.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Everyone has their own learning style and strengths. Find the method that suits you, and don't lose heart when a friend is better at one subject.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Be yourself in love. Someone who truly cares for you will treasure the real you, with no need to pretend.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Don't spend to keep up with others. Living within your means and being content with what you have keeps your finances steady.

loiKhuyen: Write down three of your strengths and remind yourself of them whenever you feel discouraged.
ghiChu: This verse is for reflection, to help you look within; it is not a prediction.

tho: The roof is old, yet keeps us dry
While rain sweeps past and storms go by
Boiled greens, clear soup: a humble meal
Let rain pour down; it's love we feel
loiGiai: A roof need not be new; it only needs people beneath it who still shelter one another. Storms outside can be fierce, but when the family sits down to a shared meal, every heart settles. This verse reminds you that your strongest support is often right beside you: a kind question, a meal together, a moment of giving way. A home is kept by small things done faithfully every day.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: Harmony at home grows when each person yields a little. Eat together, put the phones away, and ask after one another sincerely.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Work can pile up like rain on the porch. Try not to carry all of it home; once you reach the door, let yourself rest.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Restful sleep and wholesome home meals are the base of good health. If tiredness lingers, see a doctor for peace of mind.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: A tidy study corner at home helps you focus. Encouragement from family is a great strength, so share your struggles.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Love lasts when two people build a home on respect. Listen to each other more than you argue over who is right.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Money goes further when the household plans together. Talking openly about spending prevents misunderstandings.

loiKhuyen: Today, share a full meal with your loved ones and ask one heartfelt question.
ghiChu: This verse is for reflection, to help you look within; it is not a prediction.

tho: The kitchen fire is small but true
Its embers warm the whole day through
We gathered wood while days were fair
So winter finds the pot still there
loiGiai: A kitchen fire need not roar; it only needs to be kept steady. Whoever gathers firewood while the sun still shines will have a warm meal when the cold comes. This verse asks you to live in moderation, care for what you already have, and set something aside for harder days. Plenty doesn't come from one windfall but from many small, patient gatherings.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: The one who tends the stove keeps the warmth of the home. Thank whoever cooks for you, and lend a hand in the kitchen now and then.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Steady effort beats a burst of energy followed by exhaustion. Break work into small parts and do a little each day.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Eat in moderation, favor home cooking and plenty of greens. Keep warm when the weather turns cold.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Knowledge is like dry firewood: gathered daily, it becomes plenty. Review regularly instead of cramming before exams.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Affection is kept warm by small daily care, not by grand words or expensive gifts.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Your means are modest but sufficient. Save regularly and build an emergency fund; avoid impulsive spending.

loiKhuyen: Set aside a small amount each week for the day you will need it, however little.
ghiChu: This verse is for reflection, to help you look within; it is not a prediction.

tieuDe: The Lamp at the Lane's End
tho: A lamp at the lane's end glows gold
Guiding late walkers through the cold
Learning is such a gentle light
Lit bit by bit, it grows more bright
loiGiai: One small lamp at the end of a lane is enough to keep night walkers from stumbling. What you know is the same: it need not dazzle, only be lit steadily, so it lights your own way and helps others too. This verse encourages you to start with small things, learn a little at a time, work piece by piece, and gladly share what you know.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: You can be a lamp for your family: timely advice, a helping hand offered before anyone asks.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Share your experience with colleagues. Helping others understand the work deepens your own understanding.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Work in good light and rest your eyes after long stretches in front of a screen.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Study a little every day without skipping. Explaining a lesson to a friend is the best way to remember it.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Sincerity is like a warm lamp: not glaring, yet it makes people want to stop by. Simply be yourself, kindly.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Income grows with skill. Investing in learning is the surest investment of all.

loiKhuyen: Pick one small skill, practice it fifteen minutes a day, then share it with someone who needs it.
ghiChu: This verse is for reflection, to help you look within; it is not a prediction.

tho: At dawn the pagoda bell rings clear
And calls you gently: morning's here
Eat well, sleep deep the whole night long
A quiet heart keeps the body strong
loiGiai: The morning bell hurries no one; it simply reminds us that a new day has come. This verse points to health: the body needs a steady rhythm, wholesome food, enough sleep, and a few minutes of slow breathing. When the body is cared for, the mind settles more easily; when the mind is at peace, every task feels lighter. Don't wait until you are worn out to rest; keep your rhythm starting today.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: The family might rise early together, take a walk or share breakfast. A steady rhythm makes home life more pleasant.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Begin the workday with a few quiet minutes and put the important tasks first, rather than rushing in the moment you wake.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Go to bed and get up at regular times, move gently in the morning. If symptoms persist, see a doctor.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: The mind is clear in the morning, a good time for difficult lessons. Afterwards, stand up, stretch and drink some water.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: A sincere good-morning message can brighten someone's whole day. Love also needs a steady rhythm, like breathing.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Spend in moderation as you eat in moderation. Note down your expenses this week to see where you stand.

loiKhuyen: Tomorrow, try waking ten minutes earlier and take five slow breaths before the day begins.
ghiChu: This verse is for reflection, to help you look within; it is not a prediction.

tho: I light a stick at morning's start
For those who built this home and heart
Its fragrance drifts beyond the door
From thankful roots, sweet blossoms pour
loiGiai: Lighting a stick of incense is a moment to remember those who gave you today: grandparents, parents, teachers, even people whose names you never knew. Gratitude needs no grand ritual, only to be spoken and turned into deeds. This verse reminds you to honor where you came from; a grateful heart softens, and the relationships around you grow gentler too.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: Call your grandparents or parents. A simple thank-you warms the hearts of those you love.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Acknowledge the efforts of those you work with. Timely thanks bring a team closer together.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Be grateful to the body that carries so much for you, and repay it with good sleep and wholesome meals.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Remember the teachers and mentors who guided you. Studying diligently is the most practical way to thank them.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Don't take your loved one's care for granted. Say thank you, even for little things.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Value the money you earn and spend thoughtfully. Knowing what is enough is already half of wealth.

loiKhuyen: Today, say thank you to three people, one of them someone in your own home.
ghiChu: This verse is for reflection, to help you look within; it is not a prediction.

tho: The tea has cooled upon the tray
Its fragrance gently slipped away
Let go of longing, rest your mind
Brew fresh, and leave the cold behind
loiGiai: Once a cup of tea has cooled, its first warmth is hard to find again. Some things in life are like that: they have passed, and holding on only weighs the heart down. This verse asks you to cherish what was, then gently set it down. Boiling fresh water and brewing a new cup means giving yourself the chance to start again with a clearer spirit.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: Old family matters are behind you; don't bring them up to blame each other. Start again with a gentle word.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: If a project failed or a chance slipped away, take the lesson and move on; don't let it hold you back too long.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Lingering sadness affects sleep and health. Talk with someone you trust, or seek a professional when needed.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: One poor exam doesn't define you. Review your mistakes, then keep studying with a fresh mind.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: If a bond has cooled, thank it and let it go in peace. A lighter heart is ready to welcome someone who truly fits.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Don't try to win back a loss by taking risks. Calmly start again and spend more carefully.

loiKhuyen: Write down one thing you still regret, read it once, then tell yourself: I allow myself to move on.
ghiChu: This verse is for reflection, to help you look within; it is not a prediction.

tho: The road winds over hill on hill
Don't fear the climb; sit, rest, be still
When work feels lost, look back a while
You've come so far, mile after mile
loiGiai: A road over the hills is never straight; some stretches climb, some wind about, but whoever keeps walking will arrive. This verse is for anyone who feels their work is slow and the results unseen. Don't rush to compare yourself with others; look back at the distance you have already come and keep your pace. Patience isn't standing still, but walking on before the destination is in sight.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: Family members need time to understand one another. Don't expect everything to change after one conversation.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Your work is on an uphill stretch. Set small weekly goals and note your progress to see that you are still moving.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Recovery takes time. Follow your doctor's guidance and don't abandon treatment out of impatience.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Some subjects are steep hills. Break the lessons into small pieces and ask teachers or friends when stuck.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Love need not race ahead. Walk together slowly to truly know each other.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Income rises slowly but surely if you persevere. Steer clear of get-rich-quick offers.

loiKhuyen: Write down three things you accomplished last month to see that you have come further than you think.
ghiChu: This verse is for reflection, to help you look within; it is not a prediction.

tho: A door left just ajar, not wide
Lets spring and morning sun inside
Keep your heart warm, serene and true
An honest heart lets love come through
loiGiai: A door left ajar is neither locked nor flung wide: it guards itself while still ready to welcome. This verse speaks of love and connection. Don't lock your heart because of one hurt, yet don't give everything before you truly know each other. Live gently and sincerely; the person who suits you will recognize that warmth.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: Open up to your family and say what you think, rather than keeping it inside and feeling sad alone.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Welcome feedback from colleagues with an open mind. A new door may open from a single conversation.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Open the windows for fresh air and open your heart too. Meeting friends keeps the spirit healthy.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Be willing to learn from others, even those younger than you. The door of understanding opens when we are no longer too shy to ask.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Good bonds come when you are ready and sincere. Give each other time; neither rush nor close your heart.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Think carefully when someone asks you to invest or lend money. A door both open and secure keeps your savings safe.

loiKhuyen: Reach out to a friend you haven't contacted in a while, just to ask how they have been.
ghiChu: This verse is for reflection, to help you look within; it is not a prediction.

tho: The staircase rises, stair by stair
Rush, and you'll trip, so climb with care
So learning climbs in quiet ways
One step each day through all your days
loiGiai: No one climbs a staircase in a single leap. The steady climber takes each step in turn, hand firm on the rail, without hurry. This verse advises you, in study and work alike, to follow the right order: master the basics before going far. Quiet progress each day adds up, carrying you to places that once seemed far too high.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: Help the young ones at home grow step by step; praise small efforts instead of demanding big results at once.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Advancement needs a firm base. Do the task at hand well and keep learning; opportunity follows ability.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Increase exercise gradually without straining. Taking the stairs instead of the elevator is gentle daily movement.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Master the fundamentals before the hard parts. Solve a few problems every day, steadily rather than in bursts.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Love has its steps too: meeting, understanding, caring, then committing. Skip none of them.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Save in small increments. A realistic savings goal is easier to keep than one set too high.

loiKhuyen: Set yourself one small goal you can finish this week, and see it through completely.
ghiChu: This verse is for reflection, to help you look within; it is not a prediction.

tho: Brick upon brick, the house will stand
Lay each one firm with careful hand
Don't rush to borrow; build with care
Within your means, with meals to share
loiGiai: A sturdy house isn't built in a day but from bricks laid with care. Wealth is the same: work diligently, spend with a plan, and don't borrow beyond your means. This verse advises going slowly but surely; don't place a heavy burden on your shoulders just to have things sooner. A peaceful home is worth more than a large house with an uneasy heart.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: Let the whole family contribute and discuss big decisions together. With everyone doing their part, the home stands firm.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Build your reputation bit by bit through reliable, careful work. Trust is the most lasting brick of all.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Don't overwork from money worries. Health is the foundation; once damaged, it is hard to repair.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Knowledge is built like a brick wall: the lower rows must be firm for the upper ones to hold. Don't skip old lessons.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Build together and plan for the long term. Be open with each other about money from the start.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Make a clear savings plan, borrow only when truly needed and within your ability to repay. No gambling, no chasing promises of high returns.

loiKhuyen: Track your income and spending for a month, then choose one unnecessary expense to cut.
ghiChu: This verse is for reflection, to help you look within; it is not a prediction.

tieuDe: The Wheel That Keeps Its Pace
tho: The wheel rolls on at steady pace
Uphill, it never tries to race
When tasks pile high, don't rush or fret
One at a time, they'll all be met
loiGiai: A wheel travels far by turning evenly, not by spinning fast. On a slope, a skilled rider doesn't pedal wildly but keeps the rhythm. This verse is for times when work piles up: don't panic, and don't juggle five things at once until none is done well. Set an order, finish one task at a time, rest when it is time. A steady pace will carry you over the hill.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: Share the housework so each person has a part and no one carries it all. The home then runs as smoothly as a round wheel.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: List your tasks by priority and finish each one before the next. Avoid taking on more than you can handle.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Keep a steady daily rhythm for meals, sleep and exercise. The body thrives when life has a pace.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Make a realistic timetable and follow it. Studying a little daily works better than staying up all night.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Love needs steadiness more than moments of passion followed by coolness. Care for each other a little every day.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Steady income calls for steady spending. Avoid risky investments that throw your finances off balance.

loiKhuyen: Choose the three most important tasks today and finish them one by one before looking at anything else.
ghiChu: This verse is for reflection, to help you look within; it is not a prediction.

tho: By the window, Mother sews
Each tiny stitch with love she sows
Small stitches, humble as can be
Keep those who travel warm and free
loiGiai: A thread is thin, yet it can stitch a coat that keeps one warm all winter. Love at home often shows itself in very small things: a stitch, a meal kept warm, a word of caution. This verse reminds you to notice and cherish the invisible thread that ties you to your family. Don't let busyness wear that thread thin.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: Look back on the small things your family has done for you. Make time to visit and listen to your parents' stories.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Care in each small task is what makes quality. Don't overlook details that seem to go unnoticed.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Keep warm and dress well when it is cold. Caring for yourself also puts your loved ones at ease.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Study is like sewing: even stitches make a fine seam. Be careful with each small lesson.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: The thread between two people is small daily care. A caring question is sometimes worth more than a big gift.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Look after your belongings and mend instead of throwing away. Saving starts with the smallest things.

loiKhuyen: Call or visit your mother, father, or whoever cared for you, and say thank you.
ghiChu: This verse is for reflection, to help you look within; it is not a prediction.

tho: The mirror shows the face you bear
The heart alone shows what is there
Own each mistake and mend it right
Learn like soft rain, from morn to night
loiGiai: A mirror shows only your face; your heart you must look into yourself. This verse invites you to pause and look at yourself honestly: what you do well, and what still falls short. Recognizing a mistake isn't for self-blame but for correction. Whoever learns from their own mistakes keeps improving steadily, like light rain soaking deep into the soil.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: When there is friction, ask where you went wrong before blaming others. An apology can untie many knots.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Review how you work and find one point to improve. Ask someone you trust for a clearer view.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Listen to your body: fatigue, pain and sleeplessness are all signals. Regular check-ups help you know yourself better.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Go over your wrong answers and note common mistakes. Understanding why is worth more than copying the right solution.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Before asking someone to change, look at how you have treated them. Be honest with yourself first, then with others.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Look honestly at your spending habits. Knowing where your money goes is the first step to keeping it.

loiKhuyen: At day's end, take five minutes to ask: what did I do well today, and what do I want to improve tomorrow?
ghiChu: This verse is for reflection, to help you look within; it is not a prediction.

tho: Beneath the eaves on summer noon
Pause, hear the breeze's gentle tune
There is no race in all you do
Rest well, and seasons strengthen you
loiGiai: At noon under a hot sun, the traveler who rests beneath the eaves is the one who can walk far. This verse reminds you that rest isn't laziness but part of endurance. Are you pushing yourself too hard? Allow yourself to stop for a moment, sip some water, listen to the wind. Keep your health, and everything else remains possible.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: Spend a whole afternoon with your family without talking about work. Resting together is also a way of growing closer.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: You need not win every contest. Working with regular breaks is more effective and leads to fewer mistakes.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Drink enough water, avoid harsh sun, take a short nap if you can. If fatigue persists, see a doctor.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Study for about forty-five minutes, then rest for ten. A relaxed mind remembers better.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Give each other quiet space to breathe. You need not always talk; sitting side by side is warm enough.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Don't work overtime to the point of exhaustion for a small sum. Health is the greatest capital you have.

loiKhuyen: Give yourself a real break today: silence your phone notifications for at least thirty minutes.
ghiChu: This verse is for reflection, to help you look within; it is not a prediction.

tho: A straw fire flares, then fades away
The coals glow on throughout the day
So too with wealth: take no wild chance
Save bit by bit, with slow advance
loiGiai: A straw fire blazes up and dies quickly, while coals smolder and keep warm all afternoon. This verse speaks of money: profits that come too fast rarely last, while money earned by your own effort and saved month by month is a lasting support. Stay clear-headed before promises of quick riches, and be patient with the slow, sure path of saving.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: Agree as a family on how to spend, so no one makes large decisions alone without discussion.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Choose steady, lasting work over opportunities that sound exciting but are vague.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Don't keep working late nights to earn fast. When health wears down, money is hard to keep too.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Cramming is a straw fire, forgotten after the exam. Real understanding is the coal that keeps burning.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Love that flares too quickly cools quickly. Let a relationship grow through time and understanding.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: No gambling, no investing on tempting promises of high returns. Save steadily, a little each month, and it will become capital.

loiKhuyen: Before putting money into anything, wait three days and ask the opinion of someone knowledgeable you trust.
ghiChu: This verse is for reflection, to help you look within; it is not a prediction.

tieuDe: The Late Lamp by the Book
tho: A late lamp by a weighty book
A page a day, a careful look
When night grows deep, close it and rest
By morning, lessons shine their best
loiGiai: A lamp beside an open book is an image of diligent study. But diligence doesn't mean staying up all night; study a little each day, close the book when it is time and sleep, and the mind will be clear by morning. This verse encourages perseverance in learning while guarding your strength. Truly understanding one page is better than skimming a whole book.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: The family could read together a little each evening. A reading habit shared at home is a lasting gift.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Set aside time each week to learn more about your trade. New knowledge brings confidence at work.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Frequent late-night study harms the eyes and sleep. Set a fixed bedtime and keep to it.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Read slowly, note the main ideas, and review them the next morning. A little each day, without skipping a day.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Reading the same book and sharing your thoughts is a way to understand each other more deeply.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Spending on learning is worthwhile. Good books need not be costly; the library door is always open.

loiKhuyen: Tonight, read one page carefully, write down one good idea, then go to bed on time.
ghiChu: This verse is for reflection, to help you look within; it is not a prediction.

tho: The evening bell rings down the lane
Then fades on wind across the plain
Held anger brews a storm inside
Let go, like echoes fading wide
loiGiai: The evening bell rings far and then dissolves into the air, holding on to nothing. This verse speaks of letting go: anger and resentment kept inside for long grow heavy as stone. Letting go doesn't mean forgetting everything or accepting unfairness; it means not letting old matters hurt you further. When the heart grows lighter, everything around you seems gentler.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: After a quarrel at home, let a night pass so tempers cool, then talk in a gentle voice.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: A criticism or a misunderstanding: take the lesson and let it pass. Don't carry it all week.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Long-term stress affects sleep and digestion. Try slow breathing, walking, or talking with a professional if needed.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: If an exam went poorly, be sad for a little while, then let it go. Save your energy for the next lesson.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: When upset, speak gently instead of letting it build up. Forgiveness keeps peace for you both.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Grieving over what was lost only weighs the heart. Accept it, learn from it, and rework your spending plan.

loiKhuyen: When your heart feels heavy, sit still, breathe slowly ten times and silently say: I set this down.
ghiChu: This verse is for reflection, to help you look within; it is not a prediction.

tho: When winds are still, the smoke climbs high
So upright hearts don't twist or lie
Trade honestly, and have no fear
Keep every promise, whole and clear
loiGiai: On a windless day, incense smoke rises straight up, untangled. That is simply nature, not an omen; it is only an image to help you look into your own heart. An honest person is the same: with nothing to hide, the heart is light and one walks tall anywhere. This verse advises keeping your word in work and money matters. Keep even small promises, finish even small tasks completely. Over time people will trust you, and that trust is the most precious capital.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: Be straightforward with your family and don't hide important matters. Openness keeps harmony for the long run.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Keep appointments and say what is true. When wrong, admit it and correct it; your reputation will grow.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: A life with nothing to hide brings good sleep and good appetite. A light mind is part of a healthy body.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Do your work by your own effort, without cheating. Honest results show you what you still need to learn.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Love lasts when both are sincere. Don't promise what you cannot do.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Money earned honestly is money kept long. Repay loans on time and deal fairly in every trade.

loiKhuyen: Complete one small promise you made to someone that is still unfinished.
ghiChu: This verse is for reflection, to help you look within; it is not a prediction.

tho: A cup of tea we pour and share
Kind words like cool rain in the air
Few words, but warm, can mean much more
True hearts make tea worth waiting for
loiGiai: Pouring tea for someone is a way of saying you value them. This verse focuses on speech: a gentle word can cool a whole hot day, while harsh words are hard to take back. Speak little but truly, slowly but warmly. When your words carry respect, the relationships around you naturally grow closer.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: At home, speak to one another as gently as you would to a guest. Your family deserves your kindest manner.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Give feedback to colleagues with soft, clear words. Tactful speech helps work run smoothly.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Drink warm tea and slow down for a few minutes. Small pauses bring ease to the mind.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Ask teachers and friends with humility, and you will receive generous help.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Words of love need not be many, only true. Avoid harsh words when angry; wait until calm to speak.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Make deals and agreements with clear, courteous words. Friendly dealings keep customers for years.

loiKhuyen: Today, offer someone a cup of tea or a glass of water, and listen more than you speak.
ghiChu: This verse is for reflection, to help you look within; it is not a prediction.

tho: At the crossroads, unsure, you wait
Ask those ahead, then weigh each gate
Know your own strength, consider well
Once chosen, walk through rain and swell
loiGiai: When you stand at a fork in the road, hesitation is natural. This verse advises against choosing while confused: ask those who have gone before, consider your strengths, weigh what you truly need. No choice is perfect, but some choices fit. And once you have chosen, walk on with your whole heart instead of always looking back at the other road.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: Discuss big family matters together. Listen to each person before deciding.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Considering a new job or project? List the gains and losses, ask someone experienced, then decide.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: When unsure about treatment, ask your doctor, and consider a second opinion from another specialist.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Choose a field or school based on your real interests and abilities, not just the crowd.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Don't make decisions about love when overly happy or sad. Give your heart time to settle.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Before a large expense, compare carefully and ask if you really need it. Choose the safe option within your means.

loiKhuyen: Write both options on paper with three gains and three losses each, and sleep on it before deciding.
ghiChu: This verse is for reflection, to help you look within; it is not a prediction.

tieuDe: The Window Open to the Breeze
tho: At dawn I open wide the pane
Cool breezes come, and sun again
Too long you've sat before the screen
Stand up and walk the gentle green
loiGiai: A room shut too long grows stuffy; open the window and cool wind and morning sun pour in. Body and mind need opening like this: go outside and move about, breathe fresh air, meet family and friends. This verse advises you to spend less time closed within four walls or in front of a screen. A little movement and a little morning sunlight will help you feel healthier and happier.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: Air out the house, tidy up together, add a green plant or two. A bright home makes for easier hearts.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: When stuck, step away from your desk for a few minutes. Fresh ideas often come when the mind is clear.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Take a gentle walk each morning, get some early sun, keep your bedroom airy. See a doctor early for breathing problems.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Study where there is natural light, and now and then look into the distance to rest your eyes.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Open up to group activities and meet new friends. Connections come when you step outside.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Opening a window costs nothing. Many simple joys are free.

loiKhuyen: Tomorrow morning, open every window, walk outside for fifteen minutes and notice three beautiful things.
ghiChu: This verse is for reflection, to help you look within; it is not a prediction.

tho: The old step wears its moss with grace
Where parents wait to see your face
Come home and share a humble meal
Sit by the lamp, say how you feel
loiGiai: The front step of the old house is where parents wait for their children to come home, where your childhood ran in and out. This verse reminds you not to let work sweep you so far away that you forget the way back. Your family needs no grand gifts; they only wish to see your face, share a meal and hear a few stories. Time together is a gift nothing can replace.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: Plan a visit home, or video call your grandparents and parents. Listen to their old stories with full patience.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: However busy you are, keep time for family. Work will still be there, but moments together wait for no one.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Watch over your parents' health and remind them of regular check-ups. Take elders to the doctor if something seems wrong.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: If you study far from home, stay in touch with family. Their encouragement helps you stand firm.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: When the relationship is serious, bring your partner home to meet the family. Respecting each other's family is the base of lasting love.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Filial love isn't measured in money brought home. Spend sensibly and help your family within your means.

loiKhuyen: This week, set a day to visit or have a long call with your parents or grandparents.
ghiChu: This verse is for reflection, to help you look within; it is not a prediction.

tho: The wheel sinks deep in muddy ground
Lay straw and stones, pull slow and sound
When money's tight, spend not in haste
Track every coin, and nothing waste
loiGiai: When a wheel sinks into mud, pushing harder only sinks it deeper. The skillful one stops, lays down stones, ties a rope and pulls slowly. This verse is for times of financial difficulty: don't panic into high-interest loans or reckless moves to recover. Calmly write down your income and expenses, cut what isn't yet needed, and ask a trusted family member for advice. Climb out bit by bit, slowly but surely.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: When the family faces hardship, discuss together how to get through without blaming. United, the burden feels lighter.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: When work hits an obstacle, don't simply push harder. Stop to find the cause and ask colleagues for help.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Money worries can steal your sleep. Share them with family and keep regular sleep and meals.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: If there are gaps in your knowledge, go back to where you lost track, like stones under the wheel, then move forward.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Shared hardship tests the heart. Plan together and be honest with each other about your situation.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Avoid high-interest loans and never gamble to win money back. Make a budget, put essentials first and repay debts steadily by plan.

loiKhuyen: Sit down and list all of this month's income and expenses, then cross off one item that can wait.
ghiChu: This verse is for reflection, to help you look within; it is not a prediction.

tho: If thread gets tangled, have no fear
Don't pull; find where the ends appear
When hearts are knotted, go with care
Speak gently, and love loosens there
loiGiai: Yank a tangled thread and it only knots tighter; you must patiently find the end and loosen it loop by loop. Matters of love and family are the same. When misunderstandings pile up, don't insist on having your say or on who wins. Calmly find where it all began, speak slowly and listen fully. Once the first knot is undone, the rest come easier.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: Family conflicts need to be untied one at a time. Choose a moment when everyone is calm to sit and talk.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: When work is tangled, list everything on paper and find the root task to handle first. Don't tackle it all at once.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: When your mind is in a muddle, sleep on it or take a walk. A healthy spirit untangles things more wisely.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: A hard problem is like a tangled thread: reread the question, find the key facts, and solve it step by step.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Misunderstandings between two people aren't untied with harsh words. Ask to understand, speak to be understood, and be patient.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: If debts are muddled, write each one down and decide which comes first. Clarity is the first step to a lighter load.

loiKhuyen: Pick one small misunderstanding, arrange to talk with the other person, and at first only ask and listen.
ghiChu: This verse is for reflection, to help you look within; it is not a prediction.

tho: The mirror clouds with dust of years
Wipe just a little: light appears
Each day, wipe one small corner clear
Unsought, a quiet peace draws near
loiGiai: A mirror left alone gathers dust, not because it is a bad mirror but because dust drifts in every day. The heart is like this: worries, irritation and fatigue settle bit by bit. This verse advises you to set aside a small moment each day to wipe the heart clean: sit still, breathe slowly, let go of what need not be kept. A clear heart sees things clearly, and lives more lightly and peacefully.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: Don't let small annoyances pile up into distance. Each night, say something pleasant to one another before sleep.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Clear your desk, sort your inbox, drop tasks that aren't needed. Outer order brings a clearer mind.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Spend ten minutes each day in stillness and breathing. Sleep enough, and if stress lingers, seek a professional.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Review old lessons often, like wiping a mirror, and your knowledge will stay clear instead of fading.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Set aside old prejudices and see your loved one with fresh eyes. A clear heart sees the good in each other.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Review your recurring expenses and cancel services you no longer use. Tidy finances lighten the heart too.

loiKhuyen: Tonight, sit still for five minutes, breathe slowly, and let each thought pass like dust wiped from a mirror.
ghiChu: This verse is for reflection, to help you look within; it is not a prediction.
